rule_semantics.strength_meaning: A MUST rule blocks acceptance only when it is applicable to the actual action or claim.
rule_semantics.evidence_required_meaning: The rule needs adequate evidence before its effect is accepted; this does not by itself require persistent project-state evidence.

selected_when_all: the plan step resolves to the rule route selector
the actual component object type and state satisfy scope
an event that actually occurs in the step intersects the rule trigger
all available predicates pass and no applicable exception removes the rule
activation.legacy_event_normalization: A declared facet may normalize to a frozen event token only when that facet is actually written or audited in the step; the mapping records provenance and never selects a rule directly.

decomposed_request_semantics.raw_request: The unchanged user request is the Agent's semantic source and is hash-preserved; deterministic scripts validate the resulting plan and do not keyword-classify the prose.
decomposed_request_semantics.mode_uniqueness: One execution mode is selected and held stable per plan step; a decomposed request may contain multiple step-local modes.
decomposed_request_semantics.write_route_uniqueness: Each writing step must have a conflict-free executable route; this does not limit the whole request to one writing step, one route, or one file.
decomposed_request_semantics.authorization: The union of step-local writes must remain inside the complete user request boundary.
decomposed_request_semantics.multi_step_continuation: A natural-language request may close one checkpoint and continue into later authorized steps without a second user command or standard phrase.
decomposed_request_semantics.no_one_step_gate: Step decomposition is an internal dependency model, not a requirement to stop after each step.

window_recovery_policy.purpose: Recovery level determines the amount of project material that must be read to regain trustworthy context. ChangeSet propagation and project invalidation are separate concerns.
window_recovery_policy.r0_allowed_only_when: window_context=same_window and all same_window_requires conditions are proven

baseline_contract.meaning: A trusted full-project snapshot index, not a project copy, handoff summary, partial watch-root manifest, or field-presence flag.
baseline_contract.state_shape: workspace_baseline remains the path-to-sha256-and-size map; workspace_baseline_meta carries qualification and provenance. The meta object is optional for legacy load but all listed bindings are required whenever it exists.

window_recovery_policy.source: V8 R0_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINT requires same uninterrupted session; new window or context recovery must not use R0. V7/V8 R2 supplies the full-project read contract; V16 restores it only after an R2 trigger.

natural_pause.mixed_request: An explicit checkpoint close followed by pause is one ordered G2 then G1 plan and needs no extra user confirmation.

g1.allowed_continuation: implement and validate every declared target in one uninterrupted working flow

g2.evidence: fresh replacements only for explicitly affected post-specification levels
g2.unaffected_prefix: reuse current scope through selection_rationale without copying or rerecording it
g2.consumer_policy: exact declared effects and file/command/artifact identity bindings; optional claim_updates bind SHA-256 identities of old/new producer evidence claim text and close only their exact producers and typed consumers, with no coarse transitive invalidation
g2.prefix_identity_guard: live-validate every reused target prefix record before reconciliation
g2.source_anchor: live-validate the source question lifecycle evidence and semantically recover its implementation plus E1/E2 in a new window
g2.identity_closed_world: every actual protected registered identity delta must be declared in the ChangeSet and artifact_updates; all changed file/command locators and artifact input refs are scanned globally and fresh replacement locators must lie in the ChangeSet
g2.working_identity_scope: an unrelated unprotected working artifact with no exact evidence binding does not block the batch
g2.component_snapshot: preserve state, status, and invalidated_at_revision for targets and source

escalate_when: the model contract, candidate set, selection rationale, objective, constraints, feasible domain, assumptions, or claim boundaries changed
an exact affected consumer lies outside the declared closure
a reused prefix or source evidence locator no longer matches its live identity
an actual protected registered identity delta is omitted or lies outside the sealed ChangeSet
a changed exact evidence binding or fresh replacement locator lies outside the sealed ChangeSet

an explicitly changed claim has a producer or typed consumer outside the declared effect closure, conflicts with producer claim-text identity, or an in-closure replacement does not bind its new identity
a target or source state, status, invalidation marker, or execution revision drifts before reconciliation
fresh equivalence or implementation evidence fails or is missing

recovery_execution_barrier.open_when: the effective recovery level is R2_FULL and its single recovery episode is not closed_ready or closed_blocked

identity_reconstruction.rebuild_command_meaning: Commands that enumerate, hash, parse, or compare existing evidence; never an implicit solver or verifier run.
identity_reconstruction.missing_evidence_policy: Record the exact gap and blocked or invalidated status; do not manufacture a pass by rerunning business computation.

recovery_execution_barrier.full_read_is_not_a_second_runtime_grant: An R2_FULL assessment, including an explicit user full-recovery request, authorizes only the safe read/enumerate/hash/parse/compare work defined by r2_protocol; it does not need a second full_project_audit grant and does not authorize project execution.

dangerous_runtime_actions.direct_request_anchor: Exact user-request excerpt is retained without keyword classification.
dangerous_runtime_actions.purpose: Prevent the Agent from turning control actions into undeclared solver, verifier, recomputation, full-audit, or Skill-package commands.

G0_ADVISORY.purpose: answer, explain, plan, or perform a non-state-dependent read-only review

G1_WORKING.purpose: ordinary scoped project work, including a multi-file change set

G2_CHECKPOINT.purpose: state transition, frozen decision, milestone identity, or scoped acceptance claim

closure.local: changed semantic facets plus their direct claim, reference, terminology, figure, and layout consumers
closure.component: the affected component and evidence that explicitly binds changed identities
closure.checkpoint: the exact required evidence set for the requested transition or acceptance claim
closure.release: all declared deliverables and their registered reproducibility and provenance dependencies
full_project_scope_only_when: the user explicitly requests a full-project audit
the declared G3 delivery scope is the whole project
an R2_FULL recovery episode is active
R2_full_recovery_only_when: the user explicitly requests full recovery
authoritative project state is missing or corrupt and the requested action depends on it
the project-root identity conflicts with the authoritative state
the workspace baseline is missing stale incomplete or ineligible
a relevant change cannot be localized or attributed
the complete transitive consumer closure cannot be proven
an R1_TARGETED episode discovers a relevant object outside its proven scope
closure.G3_scope_audit: G3 audits the exact declared release scope. G3 by itself neither expands that scope to the whole workspace nor classifies recovery as R2_FULL.

hard_blocks: the user has not authorized the affected mutation or promotion
an actual requested state transition is illegal
a frozen identity or decision would change without the required decision
an applicable MUST acceptance condition fails within the affected closure
a real same-dimension conflict cannot be resolved by scope, evidence, refinement, or supersession
a G2 or G3 claim lacks required current exact-bound evidence
not_hard_blocks: the user did not use internal standard vocabulary
one clause in a mixed request needs clarification while independent clauses are executable
an unrelated working file is unregistered or dirty
a G1 edit has no persistent execution ledger or start/end receipt
an atom evidence schema is not materialized during ordinary G1 work
a local change does not satisfy rules that are outside its actual semantic closure
an internal multi-step plan has completed one step and later already-authorized steps remain
ordinary reading, editing, compiling, rendering, or scoped checks have no dangerous runtime-action grant
